description: In a groundbreaking initiative in New Orleans, discarded glass bottles are being turned into sand for coastal restoration. Known as Glass Half Full, this program has successfully redirected millions of pounds of glass from local landfills. Current research is examining the positive impact of this recycled glass sand on the growth and durability of wetland vegetation, providing a creative solution to Louisiana's ongoing coastal land loss issues.

title: Washington couple spent $300,000 on home plans; state wants 44 acres surrendered
description: Tyler Chambers embarked on an ambitious journey to construct his dream home in Washington. Investing nearly $300,000 into regulatory requirements and necessary studies, he was soon met with neighbor complaints that triggered additional demands. These included extensive environmental assessments and a permanent conservation deed restriction on two-thirds of his land. Undeterred by the financial and emotional strain, Chambers remains resolute in his quest to build a home.

title: Why Mark Zuckerberg's wife's school was shut down despite $125 million in donations,
description: After ten years in operation, Priscilla Chan's Primary School in East Palo Alto has shut down. Supported by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, the school was designed to provide essential services for low-income families. However, despite substantial funding, student outcomes frequently lagged behind state benchmarks. As the initiative pivots towards scientific research, this closure illustrates the difficulties faced by philanthropic educational endeavors.

title: Simone Biles’ $3M mansion: Why did she build her Texas dream home?
description: Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens’ Texas lakefront mansion is finally complete after years of planning, approvals and construction delays. The couple started designing the home in 2020 and finished it in November 2025. The reported $3 million property includes a private gym, pool, sports court, large kitchen, spa-style bathroom, laundry room and a dedicated space for their dogs.

description: Diane Keaton’s Laguna Beach home, built in 1976, was purchased by the actress for $6.6 million in 2021 and transformed before being sold for $7.9 million a year later. Now, the four-bedroom oceanfront property is back on the market for $10.3 million, with Keaton’s distinctive design touches and lighting still intact.
